title: Shemini: the eighth day (Leviticus 9:1)
hookLine: after seven days of preparation, the service begins on the eighth

lines: THE EIGHTH DAY KEEPS SHOWING UP.
cards: Seven is the number of a complete week: six days of work, one of rest, and then it starts over. Shabbat keeps that loop turning. So what's an eighth day?
In Jewish life, it keeps showing up when something new begins. A baby boy is brought into the covenant on his eighth day. The festival of Sukkot is followed by an eighth day of its own.
And this week's portion is named for it: Shemini, eighth. After a week of waiting at the door, the priests finally step through.

teach.h: THE FIRST OF NISAN: TEN CROWNS.
teach.b: It opens: "And it came to pass on the eighth day, that Moses called Aaron and his sons, and the elders of Israel." The rabbis say this was the first day of Nisan, the day the sanctuary was set up for good.

The Talmud says that day took ten crowns, the first of many things: the first day the priests served, the first day the people's offerings were brought there, the first day God's presence rested among them.

teach.h: TODAY THE LORD APPEARS TO YOU.
teach.b: Moses tells Aaron what to bring, and why: for today the LORD appears to you. Then Aaron, who has watched for seven days, does it himself for the first time: the offering for himself, the offering for the people.

teach.h: AARON LIFTS HIS HANDS AND BLESSES.
teach.b: When it's done, Aaron lifts his hands toward the people and blesses them. Rashi says this was the priestly blessing, still said in synagogues today: may the Lord bless you and keep you.

teach.h: SEVEN IS NATURE; EIGHT IS BEYOND.
teach.b: Moses and Aaron go into the tent together, come out, and bless the people again. The glory of the Lord appears to everyone.
Fire comes out and consumes the offering on the altar, and the people see it, shout for joy and fall on their faces.
Why does so much begin on an eighth day? Some teachers say seven is the natural world, complete in itself, and eight is one step beyond it: the place where the holy breaks in.

how: The priestly blessing that tradition links to Aaron's first blessing on the eighth day is still recited in synagogues by kohanim, descendants of Aaron, with hands raised toward the congregation.

o: a crown: one of the honors of that day
seventh: the day of rest that ends the week
eighth: the day the priests began to serve

practice: Think of something you've been getting ready for: a project you've researched, a call you've rehearsed, a habit you've planned, a book you bought and never opened.
You've had your seven days; picture the eighth, the first real step, not perfect, just actual. Breathe in on the preparing, and out on the beginning.

wordCard.voice: Shemini. Eighth. The portion that opens on the eighth day, when the priests' preparation ends and their service begins.
